title: Summer Road Safety in Albania: Driving Rules in Albania
excerpt: Learn the essential driving rules in Albania—seatbelts, child seats, and alcohol limits—to enjoy a safe, fine‑free summer road trip from Tirana Rinas Airport.
intro: Summer brings tourists to Albania’s stunning coast and rugged mountains, but the excitement can turn risky if you overlook local traffic laws. When you pick up your rental car from AutoConnect Rental at Tirana Rinas (TIA) Airport, a quick briefing on seatbelts, child restraints, and alcohol limits will keep your journey smooth and penalty‑free.

sections.title: Driving Rules in Albania: What Every Renter Must Follow
sections.body: Albania enforces a strict set of driving rules that apply to all vehicles, including rental cars. Seatbelts are mandatory for every occupant, front and rear, and police checkpoints are common on tourist routes during summer. Children under 12 years old or shorter than 1.5 m must use a certified child restraint system suited to their weight and height. The legal blood‑alcohol limit is just 0.1 g/l, meaning even a single drink can exceed the threshold. Knowing these driving rules in Albania before you set off will help you avoid fines and stay safe on the road.

sections.title: Seatbelt Requirements for All Occupants
sections.body: In Albania, the law requires every person inside a vehicle to wear a seatbelt, regardless of where they sit. Failure to buckle up can result in hefty fines and points on your licence. Front‑seat passengers must use the adjustable belts, while rear‑seat occupants must also secure the provided belts. During peak tourist season, police often stop cars to check compliance, especially on winding mountain passes and coastal highways. Keeping everyone strapped in not only complies with the law but dramatically reduces injury risk in the event of a collision.

sections.title: Child Seat Regulations for Young Passengers
sections.body: Children under the age of 12 or under 1.5 metres in height must be secured in an appropriate child seat. The seat must be certified for the child’s weight and height and properly installed using the vehicle’s ISOFIX anchors or seatbelt. Rental agencies, including AutoConnect, can provide baby‑carrier seats or booster seats on request, ensuring you meet the legal requirements without hassle. Forgetting a child seat can lead to fines and, more importantly, puts young passengers at serious risk during Albania’s varied terrain, from city streets to mountain roads.

sections.title: Alcohol Limits and Police Checkpoints
sections.body: Albania’s blood‑alcohol limit for drivers is a strict 0.1 g/l, effectively a near‑zero‑tolerance policy. Even a small glass of wine can push you over the limit, and the penalties include heavy fines, licence suspension, or arrest. During the summer months, police set up checkpoints along major routes such as the coastal road to Himarë and the highway toward Ksamil, routinely testing drivers for compliance. Planning ahead by designating a sober driver or using local taxis for evening outings will keep your trip enjoyable and legally safe.

tip.title: Book Child Seats Ahead of Time
tip.body: When reserving your car, ask AutoConnect Rental to install a certified baby or booster seat before you arrive. This guarantees you meet Albania’s child‑seat law and saves you the scramble of finding a suitable seat after you’ve already hit the road.

faq.question: Are child car seats mandatory in Albania?
faq.answer: Yes. Children under 12 years old or under 1.5 m in height must be secured in a certified child restraint system appropriate for their weight and height.

faq.question: What is the legal blood alcohol limit for drivers in Albania?
faq.answer: The limit is 0.1 g/l of blood alcohol, meaning even a small amount of alcohol can exceed the legal threshold.

faq.question: Is it mandatory for all passengers to wear seatbelts in Albania?
faq.answer: Seatbelts are required for every occupant, including those seated in the rear, and non‑compliance can result in fines and points on your licence.
